newsitem.title: IRAQ: UN says Iraq digs up new items at missile site.
newsitem.headline: UN says Iraq digs up new items at missile site.

text.p: Iraqis have dug up more items at a ballistic missile site near Baghdad in an effort to proof they have destroyed prohibited weapons, a U.N. official said on Sunday.

"Iraqis who are excavating at a missile site have dug up new items under the presence of our team," Roger Knight, assistant director of Baghdad's Ongoing Monitoring and Verfication Centre (OMV), told Reuters.
Knight declined to say what was found or the location of the excavations.

Iraqi bulldozers began digging at the site last Tuesday to recover what Iraq said were banned missile components destroyed and buried soon after the 1991 Gulf War that drove Baghdad's troops out of Kuwait.
"The whole process is an Iraqi initiative to prove they have destroyed all prohibited missiles," Knight said.
Under the Gulf War ceasefire, Iraq is not allowed to have weapons of mass destruction, including missiles with ranges beyond 150 km (95 miles).
The U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of scrapping the weapons suspects Iraq still has a significant number of the missiles. Baghdad denies concealing missiles.
Iraq and UNSCOM are locked in a dispute over missile engines Baghdad imported from the former Soviet Union and claims to have destroyed.

The commission wants to take missile parts it dug up last year from another site out of Iraq for analysis to prove they are not substitutes for the original engines. Baghdad rejected the request and last month the U.N Security Council censured Iraq over the issue.
Knight declined to say if Iraq had agreed to let the latest finds out of Iraq for testing.
Ten U.N. inspectors, under Michael Bordin of France, are supervising the digging and will stay in Iraq as long as excavations continue, Knight said.

U.N. inspectors must certify Iraq no longer holds banned weapons before the United Nations will lift a ban on Iraqi oil exports, other than limited sales to fund humanitarian relief that began last month.
